grief.title: The Arc of Grief
grief.subtitle: Navigating Loss & Walking Through the Valley
grief.description: Grief is not a problem to be solved; it is love with nowhere to go. Here, your pilgrimage teaches you that walking through sorrow requires patience, truth, and community.
grief.scripture: “The Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.” — Psalm 34:18

challenges.title: The First Wave
challenges.subtitle: The Weight of Sudden Absence
challenges.narrative: A message arrives with words that shatter your day: a cherished presence in your life has passed away. The room spins, air turns thin, and the instinctive temptation is either to collapse inward or pretend you are unfazed.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.” — Psalm 147:3
challenges.reflectionQuestion: When sorrow strikes, do you allow yourself to grieve, or do you flee into numbness?

choices.label: Suppress and Numb
choices.desc: Lock the door, swallow the tears, and pretend you can power through your day.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Suppressing acute grief turns tears into subterranean poison. The pain remains unaddressed, sapping your vitality.

choices.label: Lament in Prayer
choices.desc: Kneel, voice your sorrow honestly to God without sugarcoating the ache, and trust Him with your broken heart.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Lament is not the absence of faith; it is faith breathing honestly. You acknowledge the loss while anchoring your soul to God's tender presence.

choices.label: Sit with the Waves
choices.desc: Step into quiet solitude. Acknowledge that you do not have to 'fix' this ache today; allow the tears to flow without panic.
choices.reflectionOutcome: By letting the waves break upon you rather than resisting them, you learn that sorrow is a season, not a permanent prison.

choices.label: Call a Trusted Confidant
choices.desc: Pick up the phone and utter the hardest words: 'I just received devastating news, and I need someone to sit with me.'
choices.reflectionOutcome: Bearing grief in isolation magnifies the burden tenfold. By inviting another into your sorrow, you discover God's comfort through human hands.

challenges.title: The Long Silence
challenges.subtitle: When the World Moves On But You Haven't
challenges.narrative: Weeks have passed. The flowers have wilted, the cards have stopped arriving, and the world rushes past at full speed. Inside, however, the silence is deafening. You wonder if you will ever laugh again without guilt.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.” — Psalm 30:5
challenges.reflectionQuestion: How do you give yourself permission to heal at your own sacred pace?

choices.label: Isolate in Resentment
choices.desc: Resent everyone going about their cheerful days; retreat into bitter withdrawal.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Resentment toward the world's momentum only locks you in a cell of your own making. It starves your soul of the grace needed to heal.

choices.label: Anchor in the Promise of Renewal
choices.desc: Read 2 Corinthians 5:1 and meditate on the eternal sanctuary being prepared beyond this earthly tent.
choices.reflectionOutcome: When earthly permanence crumbles, eternal truth becomes your rock. You remember that this chapter is not the end of the pilgrimage.

choices.label: Practice Gentle Micro-Routines
choices.desc: Do not demand monumental breakthroughs. Make your bed, drink clean water, and breathe deeply in the morning sunlight.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Healing rarely happens in a dramatic bolt of lightning; it happens in small, faithful acts of honoring your daily breath.

choices.label: Join a Grief Support Group
choices.desc: Step into a circle of fellow wayfarers who also know the cadence of loss.
choices.reflectionOutcome: In the fellowship of shared suffering, shame vanishes. You realize you are not broken; you are merely human, walking among companions.

challenges.title: The Anniversary
challenges.subtitle: The Calendar's Quiet Ambush
challenges.narrative: The date on your calendar approaches like a storm front. Everyone expected you to have 'moved on' by now, yet the ache in your chest feels as acute as the day it happened.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.” — Psalm 23:4
challenges.reflectionQuestion: What ritual of remembrance can honor both your love and your onward calling?

choices.label: Overcompensate with Frantic Work
choices.desc: Schedule every minute of the day with tasks to drown out any possible moment of reflection.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Running from grief is like running on a treadmill—you expend immense energy without moving an inch away from the reality.

choices.label: Light a Candle and Offer Thanks
choices.desc: Dedicate an hour in quiet reverie. Thank God for the gift of their life and surrender the longing into His hands.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Transforming grief into gratitude sanctifies your memory. You honor what was lost without being devoured by despair.

choices.label: Carve Out an Unhurried Day
choices.desc: Cancel non-essential commitments. Give your soul permission to feel whatever surfaces without shame.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Patience with oneself in the valleys is the truest badge of the Wayfarer. You do not rush sacred healing.

choices.label: Share Stories with Loved Ones
choices.desc: Gather with family or friends to cook their favorite meal and recount joyful memories through laughter and tears.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Shared laughter alongside shared tears is the highest alchemy of healing. Love lives on through communion.

relationship.title: The Arc of Relationships
relationship.subtitle: Boundaries, Truth & Reconciliation
relationship.description: No armor is tested more fiercely than the human heart in proximity to others. Here, victory is not winning an argument, but preserving dignity, speaking truth with grace, and establishing holy boundaries.
relationship.scripture: “A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.” — Proverbs 15:1

challenges.title: The Heated Dinner
challenges.subtitle: Old Grievances at the Table
challenges.narrative: A family gathering starts peacefully, but a passive-aggressive barb about your life choices cuts through the air. You feel the surge of heat in your throat. Every instinct urges you to fire back with a devastating counter-strike.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.” — James 1:19
challenges.reflectionQuestion: Will your reaction defend your pride or preserve your peace?

choices.label: Retaliate with Sharp Wit
choices.desc: Expose their hypocrisy in front of everyone. Win the room, burn the bridge.
choices.reflectionOutcome: A victorious retaliatory insult leaves a bitter aftertaste. You may have won the round, but your soul is left scarred and agitated.

choices.label: Speak the Soft Answer
choices.desc: Breathe. Silently pray for grace, then reply: 'I love you too much to turn dinner into a courtroom.'
choices.reflectionOutcome: Extinguishing wrath with softness disarms aggression. You act as an ambassador of Christ's peace rather than an echo of worldly chaos.

choices.label: Take a Mindful Water Break
choices.desc: Excuse yourself calmly to get a glass of water. Allow the adrenaline to crest and recede before answering.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Ten seconds of delayed reaction can save ten months of regret. Patience is emotional sovereignty.

choices.label: Enlist an Ally's Perspective
choices.desc: Catch the eye of a calm companion at the table to de-escalate the room toward a healthier topic.
choices.reflectionOutcome: We are not called to fight family fires alone. A mature community navigates conflict with gentle diplomacy.

challenges.title: Drawing the Line
challenges.subtitle: When Saying 'Yes' is Betraying Yourself
challenges.narrative: A chronic taker in your life demands yet another emergency sacrifice of your time and emotional energy, implying that if you were truly a good Christian, you would say yes.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.” — Proverbs 4:23
challenges.reflectionQuestion: Is your accommodation motivated by genuine love, or fear of disapproval?

choices.label: Give In with Resentful Compliance
choices.desc: Say yes while grinding your teeth; complain bitterly to others afterward.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Resentful yeses are lies cloaked in piety. They poison relationships far more deeply than an honest, compassionate refusal.

choices.label: Stand in Holy Stewardship
choices.desc: Recognize that your energy is God's trust. Gently say: 'I care for you, but I cannot take this on.'
choices.reflectionOutcome: Jesus frequently withdrew from demanding crowds to pray and rest. Boundaries are not the opposite of love; they are the container that keeps love pure.

choices.label: Request Time to Discern
choices.desc: 'I will not give you a hurried answer. Let me sleep on this and reply tomorrow morning.'
choices.reflectionOutcome: Buying time breaks the cycle of manipulation. You reclaim deliberate stewardship over your schedule.

choices.label: Seek Counsel from a Mentor
choices.desc: Review the dynamic with a wise pastor or therapist before responding.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Wise counsel acts as a mirror, exposing codependent patterns and helping you walk in healthy freedom.

work.title: The Arc of Work & Purpose
work.subtitle: Self-Worth Beyond the Resume
work.description: Our labor was intended for flourishing, yet the modern workplace often reduces humans to output and metrics. In this arc, you learn to separate who you are in God from what you achieve.
work.scripture: “Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.” — Philippians 4:6

challenges.title: The Public Critique
challenges.subtitle: Under Fire in the Meeting
challenges.narrative: During a cross-team presentation, a senior stakeholder abruptly questions your competence and calls your deliverables into question in front of dozens of colleagues.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters.” — Colossians 3:23
challenges.reflectionQuestion: Is your identity anchored in the praise of mortals, or in the delight of your Creator?

choices.label: Defend Defensively with Blame
choices.desc: Blame subordinate team members and shift fault aggressively to save face.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Throwing others under the bus damages trust irrevocably and broadcasts deep insecurity to the entire room.

choices.label: Anchor Self-Worth in Christ
choices.desc: Take a breath. Remember that no slide deck defines your worth. State: 'That is valuable feedback; let us address the data together.'
choices.reflectionOutcome: When your approval is already secured by God, human criticism loses its power to terrify. You remain calm, composed, and constructive.

choices.label: Separate Tone from Substance
choices.desc: Ignore the sharp tone and extract any genuine grain of useful critique calmly.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Patience filters out the emotional noise, allowing you to salvage genuine value from hostile deliveries.

choices.label: Debrief with Trusted Colleagues
choices.desc: Meet your teammates after the session to restore morale and reaffirm mutual support.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Shared resilience turns team trials into bonded solidarity. Together you shoulder what would crush one alone.

challenges.title: The Unplanned Setback
challenges.subtitle: When the Venture Crumbles
challenges.narrative: A project you dedicated six months of evenings and weekends to is canceled with an impersonal email. The sinking feeling in your stomach whispers that you are a failure.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “For I know the plans I have for you,” declares the Lord, “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.” — Jeremiah 29:11
challenges.reflectionQuestion: Can you distinguish between a failed project and a failed human being?

choices.label: Spiral into Self-Condemnation
choices.desc: Ruminate endlessly, concluding that you are fundamentally doomed to disappoint.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Allowing an external failure to define your core worth is a spiritual tragedy. Despair robs you of tomorrow's wisdom.

choices.label: Trust God's Higher Trajectory
choices.desc: Pray: 'Lord, this closed door stings, but I trust Your redirection over my narrow plans.'
choices.reflectionOutcome: History's greatest pilgrims all walked through closed doors. Setbacks are often divine redirections toward deeper fruitfulness.

choices.label: Document Lessons Learned
choices.desc: Sit down with a journal and objectively record three skills and two insights you gained from the effort.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Nothing is wasted when extracted for wisdom. You turn disappointment into the foundation of mastery.

choices.label: Call a Seasoned Mentor
choices.desc: Hear the perspective of someone who survived similar career crashes earlier in their journey.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Mentors normalize the turbulence of life's journey, dissolving the illusion that everyone else has a smooth, effortless path.

self.title: The Arc of Self-Care & Inner Life
self.subtitle: Restoration of the Mind and Spirit
self.description: You cannot pour from an empty vessel. In this sacred arc, you confront the inner critic, dismantle exhaustion, and practice the ancient art of holy rest.
self.scripture: “Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28

challenges.title: The 3 AM Panic
challenges.subtitle: The Insomnia of Anxiety
challenges.narrative: You wake in the dead of night, heart thumping against your ribs, flooded with irrational worst-case scenarios about finances, health, and family.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.” — Psalm 56:3
challenges.reflectionQuestion: What is the small truth that can steady your breathing right now?

choices.label: Doomscroll on Your Phone
choices.desc: Stare into the blue light of social media and news feeds until your eyes burn.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Flooding an anxious nervous system with digital noise is pouring kerosene on a fire. You wake exhausted and depleted.

choices.label: The Breath of Grace
choices.desc: Inhale deeply for 4 counts: 'The Lord is my Shepherd.' Exhale for 4 counts: 'I shall not want.' Repeat until stillness descends.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Connecting physical breath to biblical truth down-regulates the sympathetic nervous system and recalibrates the spirit.

choices.label: Write a Worry Dump
choices.desc: Get out of bed, write every worry on paper, and leave the notepad in another room until morning.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Externalizing thoughts onto paper frees your mind from having to constantly loop through them.

choices.label: Text a Prayer Partner
choices.desc: Send a short message: 'Woke with anxiety tonight, please hold me in prayer when you wake.'
choices.reflectionOutcome: Knowing that you are held in intercession softens the terrifying chill of midnight isolation.

challenges.title: The Empty Well (Burnout)
challenges.subtitle: When Even Small Things Feel Crushing
challenges.narrative: A simple question like 'what do you want for dinner?' brings you to tears. Every muscle feels like lead, and you realize you have been running on fumes for months.
challenges.scriptureAnchor: “He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters, he refreshes my soul.” — Psalm 23:2-3
challenges.reflectionQuestion: Are you willing to rest before your body forces you to stop?

choices.label: Power Through with Caffeine and Guilt
choices.desc: Drink a third energy drink, berate yourself for weakness, and keep pushing.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Treating your body like an enemy will inevitably cause a catastrophic collapse. Grace honors biological reality.

choices.label: Receive Sabbath as Commandment
choices.desc: Lay down your tools. Rest is not a luxury earned by exhaustion; it is an act of trust that God runs the universe, not you.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Entering Sabbath rest is an act of deep spiritual rebellion against the idols of productivity and hurry.

choices.label: Take an Unhurried Nature Walk
choices.desc: Leave devices behind. Walk 20 minutes under the trees, noticing birds, wind, and sky.
choices.reflectionOutcome: Creation constantly sings of God's sufficiency. Immersing yourself in it resets your inner tempo.

choices.label: Ask Loved Ones to Step In
choices.desc: 'I am at my limit. Can you take care of dinner and the chores this evening?'
choices.reflectionOutcome: Vulnerability is strength. Allowing others to serve you knits community together in authentic love.

disciplines.name: The Gospel Reading
disciplines.description: Daily immersion in the words and ways of Christ. Increases clarity during spiritual trials and unlocks comforting scriptures.

disciplines.name: Reflective Journaling
disciplines.description: The practice of articulating your internal weather on paper. Helps metabolize grief and deepens emotional insight.

disciplines.name: Sacred Boundaries
disciplines.description: The fortified armor of learning to say a holy 'no' without guilt. Protects the heart from toxic emotional drain.
disciplines.buff: Reduces Resilience drain in Relationship encounters by 35%

disciplines.name: The Prayer Knot
disciplines.description: A focused discipline of continuous intercession requiring 15 Faith and 10 Community. Bestows a temporary fortitude shield.
disciplines.buff: Provides +25 Temporary Resilience before a heavy challenge

disciplines.name: The Breath of Grace
disciplines.description: A 4-4-4-4 box breathing sequence paired with scripture. Instantly calms nervous system arousal during acute anxiety.
disciplines.buff: Can be activated anytime to soothe the mind and restore Resilience

disciplines.name: The Gratitude Stone
disciplines.description: Carried in pocket or hand. A physical reminder to pause thrice daily and vocalize three specific gifts of God.

actsOfGrace.title: The Unprompted Encouragement
actsOfGrace.prompt: Send a heartfelt message of gratitude to someone who guided you during a difficult season of life, expecting nothing in return.

actsOfGrace.title: The Silent Intercession
actsOfGrace.prompt: Identify someone who irritated you recently. Spend 5 minutes in sincere prayer for their flourishing and inner peace.

actsOfGrace.title: The Unhurried Walk
actsOfGrace.prompt: Step outside for 10 minutes without your phone. Walk slowly, notice five details of God's creation, and breathe deeply.

actsOfGrace.title: The Hidden Blessing
actsOfGrace.prompt: Perform one small act of kindness anonymously—pay for someone's coffee, clean a shared space, or leave an encouraging note.
